t:
Section 2.12 of the Farm Credit Act of 1971 is amended by—

    (1) 
inserting before the period at the end of paragraph (11) “and buy from and sell to such banks interests in loans and in other financial assistance extended and nonvoting stock, as may be authorized by the Federal intermediate credit bank in accordance with regulations of the Farm Credit Administration”:
 
    (2) 
inserting before the period at the end of paragraph (13) “and when authorized by the bank participate with one or more other Farm Credit System institutions in loans made under this title or other titles of this Act on the basis prescribed in section 4.18 of this Act”; and
 
    (3) 
amending paragraph (15) to read as follows:


“(15) 
As may be authorized by the Federal intermediate credit bank in accordance with regulations of the Farm Credit Administration, agree with other Farm Credit System institutions to share loan or other losses, whether to protect against capital impairment or for any other purpose.”.

fable.w: The tempting reading treats the word "participate" and the references to "regulations of the Farm Credit Administration" as participation. But "participate" here means loan participations among Farm Credit System institutions, a financial arrangement rather than outside involvement in a federal decision. The references to FCA regulations only condition the associations' new powers on existing regulatory authority; the section does not itself require rulemaking, a comment period, a hearing, an advisory body, consultation with outsiders, or a right to sue. This is a close call because a reference to regulations could be read as implying rulemaking.
fable.s: when authorized by the bank participate with one or more other Farm Credit System institutions in loans made under this title

qwen_block.w: The section describes financial cooperation and loan participation between entities within the Farm Credit System (Federal intermediate credit banks and other Farm Credit System institutions). These are federal instrumentalities or government-sponsored enterprises, not outside parties like the general public, states, or private companies acting independently of the system. Therefore, this is internal coordination, not public participation.
qwen_block.s: participate with one or more other Farm Credit System institutions in loans made under this title

opus.w: These new powers may be used only in accordance with regulations of the Farm Credit Administration, a federal agency. The definition counts rulemaking as participation, and Example 6 counts agency rules this way. The word "participate" in paragraph (2) means lenders sharing loans with each other, not outsiders taking part in a federal decision, so it does not support the label. The section mentions governing regulations rather than directly ordering new ones, which is a weaker case than Example 6.
opus.s: as may be authorized by the Federal intermediate credit bank in accordance with regulations of the Farm Credit Administration
opus.b:
I'm labelling this **Yes**, at moderate confidence (0.6).

The tempting wrong reading is to say "Yes" because of the word "participate" in paragraph (2). That fails. There, "participate" means Farm Credit System lenders sharing in loans with each other, which is a financial arrangement and brings no outsider into a federal decision.

What does count is the reference to Farm Credit Administration regulations. That is a federal agency, and the definition counts rulemaking as participation. The section says these new loan-buying and loss-sharing powers may be used only "in accordance with regulations of the Farm Credit Administration," which assumes the agency will issue rules. Under the definition and Example 6, a statute that relies on agency rules counts as "Yes."

The reason for the lower confidence: the section mentions regulations that govern these powers rather than directly ordering the agency to write new ones, so it is arguably weaker than Example 6.

qwen_chat.w: The section describes internal operations and coordination among Farm Credit System institutions, which are federal instrumentalities. The use of the word 'participate' refers to joint lending activities between these government-related entities, not to consultation with or involvement of outside parties in a federal decision. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: participate with one or more other Farm Credit System institutions in loans made under this title or other titles of this Act on the basis prescribed in section 4.18 of this Act
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: The word "participate" appears in subsection (2) ("participate with one or more other Farm Credit System institutions in loans"), which might suggest participation. However, Farm Credit System institutions are federal instrumentalities or entities created by federal statute, and the interaction described is internal coordination among these entities regarding loan sharing. There is no involvement of outside parties (states, tribes, public, private companies outside the system) in a decision-making process. The definition explicitly excludes coordination between federal agencies or officials.
